## Welcome

This app follows the sessions of STA530 Spatial Epidemiology (University of Gothenburg, autumn 2026): from what makes data spatial, through disease maps and spatial autocorrelation, to spatial regression and Bayesian disease mapping. New sessions are added as the course goes on.

One idea runs through the course: **a map is the beginning of the epidemiologic question, not the end**. *Where* is disease high → *why* is it high there → *what* can be done?

## How to study with it

1. **Read a session.** Every topic has a status control under its heading: **Not reviewed / Reviewed / Confident**. Click as you go.
2. **Open "Before you start"** at the top of each session if a prerequisite feels rusty, and watch for the red **Common confusion** boxes.
3. **Answer the quizzes** in each session and the **why-questions** at the bottom.
4. **Practise on [Exam practice](exam-practice.qmd)**: drills that generate new numbers every time (SMR, indirect standardization, Empirical Bayes weights, box-map fences, counting neighbours, Moran's I by hand, SAR impacts, exp(β), choosing the likelihood, reading exceedance probabilities) and written exam-style questions with model answers.
5. **Check the [dashboard](dashboard.qmd)** to see what is left, in priority order.
6. Look up terms in the [glossary](glossary.qmd), or use **search** (top right).
7. **Go further** with [Resources](resources.qmd): the instructor's optional videos (Luc Anselin's spatial regression lectures), books and web pages, each linked to the section it supports.

## The exam

STA530 is examined by an **individual written exam** (2.5 credits, grades U/G/VG) and **active participation in a seminar** (1 credit, U/G). According to the lecture notes, **the exam tests concepts, not programming**. So the app focuses on explaining, interpreting and comparing; the R cells are there to build intuition, not as exam material.

## What the badges mean

No exam questions have been released yet. The badges show *why* a topic is likely to matter:

| Badge | Meaning |
|---|---|
| <span class="flag-badge flag-objective">🎯 Instructor learning objective</span> | Matches a stated learning objective: the **course syllabus**, the instructor's **Canvas post** for the session, or a **"Learning goals"** slide. Highest priority. |
| <span class="flag-badge flag-keyq">❓ Instructor's key question</span> | Answers a **key question** the instructor posted, or a question asked on a slide. |
| <span class="flag-badge flag-notes">✏️ Emphasised in class</span> | Written down as important in the **lecture notes** taken in class. |
| <span class="flag-badge flag-inferred">📌 Likely exam-relevant (AI-inferred)</span> | Inferred from definitions, formulas and worked examples on the slides. **Not confirmed by the instructor.** |
| <span class="flag-badge flag-optional">📎 Optional depth (beyond course scope)</span> | The instructor marked it as optional, or said it is not expected in STA530. |
| (no badge) | Background, examples or summaries. Still course content. |

## How to read the diagrams

Arrows mean different things in different diagrams, so every flow diagram's caption starts with its kind:

| Caption starts with | An arrow means | Example |
|---|---|---|
| **Causal diagram** | "Directly affects" | SAR vs SEM ([3.8](session3.qmd#t3-8)) |
| **Workflow** | "Then": the next step of an analysis. Not causal | From OLS to spatial regression ([3.9](session3.qmd#t3-9)) |
| **Lecture map** | How the session's ideas lead into each other. Not causal | The disease-mapping logic chain ([4.23](session4.qmd#t4-23)) |

Code blocks marked *Run Code* are interactive: R runs in your browser, no installation needed. The first run on a page takes a few seconds while R loads.
